Frank, Senior Electronics Engineer, USA
As a senior electronics engineer, I have witnessed firsthand the evolution of printed circuit boards (PCBs) from rigid substrates to increasingly flexible and adaptable forms. Flexible PCBs, or flex PCBs, represent a significant technological advancement that addresses the growing demands of modern electronics for compact, lightweight, and durable interconnections. 

In this article, I aim to explore the materials, benefits, design considerations, and diverse applications of flexible PCBs, sharing insights from both research and practical use cases in the electronics industry.
Flexible PCBs mainly use polyimide as the base material, renowned for its excellent thermal stability, mechanical flexibility, and electrical insulation properties.

articles.title: Exploring the Advantages and Applications of Flexible PCBs in Modern Electronics

articles.description:
Adam Savage Goes Behind the Scenes at the NPS Conservation Lab


Adam Savage drops in on the National Park Service’s museum conservation lab at Harpers Ferry, WV, where textile fellow Maeve O’Shea and objects fellow Daisy Greenwell walk him through the painstaking restoration of an 1860s flag. From unraveling its colorful (and mysterious) history to stabilizing fragile fibers, you’ll get a hands-on look at how the team preserves everything from textiles and paper to wood, metal, leather and even plastic artifacts from parks all over the U.S.
Heads up: the lab’s lease was canceled (yes, by Doge!) and only just got a one-year extension, so its future hangs in the balance. If you want to help keep these preservation heroes in action, plan a park visit, drop a line to your representatives, or chip in via the National Park Conservation Association.
Watch on YouTube
articles.title: Adam Savage's Tested: Adam Savage Visits the @NationalParkService Museum Conservation Lab!

🎓 College Database Management System – Oracle LiveSQL
This project demonstrates how to design and query a simple College Database using Oracle SQL on LiveSQL
Schema Design
We define four tables:
Faculty – stores teacher details.
Students – student records with department, DOB, email & phone.
Courses – subject details with credits (1–5 only).
Enrollments – junction table mapping students ↔ courses with grades.
CREATE TABLE Faculty (
CREATE TABLE Students (

✅ Here we use PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, and CHECK constraints to ensure data integrity.
Inserting Data
We add sample students, courses, and enrollments.
-- Students

meera@college.com', 9876543211);
rahul@college.com', 9876543212);
-- Courses

Queries
Now, let’s explore the data.
a) String Functions & Aggregates
👉 Converts names to uppercase & shows email length.
SELECT AVG(Credits) AS AvgCredits, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Students) AS TotalStudents
👉 Finds average course credits & total number of students.
b) Joins
👉 Displays each student with their enrolled course and grade.
c) Group By + Having
) AS StudentCount
) > 0;
👉 Shows number of students per department (only departments with students).
Views
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW StudentCoursesView AS
SELECT s.Name, c.CourseName, e.Grade
FROM Students s
JOIN Enrollments e ON s.StudentID = e.StudentID
JOIN Courses c ON e.CourseID = c.CourseID;
👉 A view gives a reusable query showing student ↔ course ↔ grade.
Stored Procedure
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE UpdateGrade(
p_StudentID IN NUMBER,
p_CourseID IN NUMBER,
p_NewGrade IN CHAR
) AS
BEGIN
UPDATE Enrollments
SET Grade = p_NewGrade
WHERE StudentID = p_StudentID AND CourseID = p_CourseID;
COMMIT;
END;
👉 Procedure to update a student’s grade in a course easily.
